第 6 章 Career Conversations as an Engineering Manager工程经理如何做职业对话

Raquel Vélez / 拉克尔·韦莱斯

— 第 28 页 —

Whether your direct report is ambitious, oblivious, or anywhere in between, your job is to help them navigate their careers. It's irrelevant where they are in their careers (e.g., early, middle, or advanced), it's in everyone's best interest to grow in a continuously challenging environment.

无论你的下属是雄心勃勃、浑然不觉，还是介于两者之间，你的工作就是帮助他们规划职业生涯。不管他们处于职业哪个阶段（早期、中期还是高级），在持续有挑战的环境中成长符合每个人的最大利益。

That said, it's not your job to create or fully outline their career paths; note that you are a guide, not a mapmaker. Your goal is to develop a trusting relationship with your reports, understanding what they want for themselves and giving them the opportunities they need to succeed.

话虽如此，你的工作不是替他们创造或完整规划职业道路；记住你是向导，不是制图师。你的目标是和下属建立信任关系，了解他们自己想要什么，并给他们成功所需的机会。

For your first career conversation with a given report, it's essential that you two get on the same page as quickly as possible. Even if you've been working together for years, it's possible that you don't know them and their motivations as well as you think you do. The sooner you identify the gaps, the sooner you can work on closing them.

和某个下属的第一次职业对话，关键是尽快达成共识。即使你们已经合作多年，你对他们和他们动机的了解可能也不如你以为的那么深。越早发现认知差距，就能越早去弥合。

The following is my framework for having productive career conversations:

以下是我进行高效职业对话的框架：

First, mention in a one-on-one that you'd like to talk about their careers. Give them the following homework:

首先，在一对一会议中提到你想聊聊他们的职业发展。给他们布置以下作业：

  • If your organization has a career path, ask them to review it and identify where they think they are on the path. If your organization does not have a career path, ask them to consider what level they think they are at and why. (And then get to work on building a career path.)如果你的组织有职业发展路径，让他们看一遍，找出自己认为自己在路径上的什么位置。如果没有，让他们思考自己认为自己在什么级别、为什么。（然后你就该去建一个职业路径了。）
  • Ask them to answer the following questions:让他们回答以下问题：
  • Do you have goals or a timeline in which you would like to reach the next level?你有没有目标或者希望什么时候达到下一个级别？
  • Are there areas that you've identified as growth areas for yourself?你有没有发现自己需要成长的方面？
— 第 29 页 —
  • Given the work that you have done so far, what would you like to keep doing? Stop doing? Start doing?就你目前做过的工作来看，你想继续做什么？停止做什么？开始做什么？
  • Have you started compiling the work you've been doing? If so, is it up to date?你有没有开始整理自己做过的工作？如果有，内容是最新的吗？

In the career conversation one-on-one, compare answers to the first homework exercise. If you're in agreement, great! Move on to the next step. If you disagree, it's time to have a deeper discussion about why you each believe you are correct. This is management, uncomfortable though it might be.

在职业对话的一对一会议中，对比第一道作业的答案。如果你们一致，太好了！进入下一步。如果不一致，那就该深入讨论一下为什么你们各自认为自己是对的。这就是管理——尽管可能让人不舒服。

After you have reached a mutual understanding of where your report is in their careers, set that as their baseline. Now move on to the second homework exercise.

当你们对下属目前的职业位置达成共识后，把它设为基线。然后进入第二道作业。

The first question is how you will gauge their understanding of how careers work. Compare their timeline with the reality of your organization. This is a great time to set expectations and avoid conflict down the road.

第一个问题是关于他们对职业发展规律的理解。把他们的时间线和你组织的现实对比一下。这是设定期望、避免未来冲突的好时机。

The second question allows the engineer to think critically about their own growth. It's important that everyone have agency over their careers, but sometimes people expect their managers to do the work for them. This is your opportunity to set the boundary: they are in charge of their careers; you are in charge of paving the way so that they can succeed. If you have also identified areas of growth for them, this is a great time to discuss it with them.

第二个问题让工程师批判性地思考自己的成长。每个人都应该对自己的职业有自主权，但有时候人们期望经理替他们干活。这是你划定边界的机会：他们掌控自己的职业；你负责铺路让他们能成功。如果你也发现了他们需要成长的方面，这是和他们讨论的好时机。

The third question gives you, the manager, a better sense of what kind of work your report likes to do. Although we all have to do "grunt work" from time to time, people do tend to be more effective in their roles when they are enjoying themselves. Use this question as an opportunity to better understand what sorts of projects your report will excel in as well as growth areas into which you can push them. This way, you can do resource planning with a purpose—you're getting the work done while also helping your reports grow!

第三个问题让你作为经理更清楚地了解下属喜欢做什么样的工作。虽然我们时不时都得干「苦活累活」，但人们在享受工作时确实表现得更好。用这个问题作为机会，更好地了解下属擅长什么类型的项目、以及你可以推动他们进入哪些成长领域。这样你就能有目的地做资源规划——既完成了工作，又帮助了下属成长！

Finally, I always ask my reports to keep track of the work they've done to date. It should include the project, relevant tasks, timeline, and impact to the team/organization/company. The purpose of this document is three-fold:

最后，我总是要求下属记录自己至今做过的工作。内容应该包括项目、相关任务、时间线、以及对团队/组织/公司的影响。这份文档有三个目的：

  1. Brains are squishy and often forget details big and small. If it's written down and shared, it's less likely that key elements of a promotion packet will be forgotten.大脑是软绵绵的，经常忘这忘那。如果写下来并分享出来，晋升材料的关键内容就不太可能被遗忘。
— 第 30 页 —
  1. You can't guarantee that you will always be their manager, and having a document that can stay with the individual engineer means that onboarding a new manager will be easier than having to start from scratch. (This is especially helpful in fast-growing companies, where an individual contributor might go through more than three or four managers in a single year!)你不能保证永远是他们的经理，而有一份可以跟着工程师本人走的文档，意味着新经理上手会比从零开始容易得多。（在快速扩张的公司里尤其有用，一个独立贡献者一年可能换三四个经理！）
  2. Finally, there's no guarantee that an employee will stay at a company for their entire careers (and is increasingly uncommon to do so). As such, an accomplishments document will be helpful when filling out resumes and helping the individual get their next position, regardless of what company they head to next.最后，没人能保证一个员工会在一家公司待一辈子（而且这越来越少见了）。因此，一份成就文档在写简历、帮人找下一份工作时会很有用，不管他们接下来去哪家公司。

That done, set a regular cadence to check in on career paths. Whether it's monthly or quarterly (yearly doesn't seem to be regular enough; weekly isn't productive), ask the same questions and check in to see whether folks are moving along the path. If you're both invested in the process, you'll see regular, incremental improvement, with the direct report in charge of their own destiny.

做完这些，设定一个固定节奏来跟进职业发展路径。无论是每月还是每季度（每年似乎不够频繁；每周又太频繁没效率），问同样的问题，看看大家是否在沿路径前进。如果你们都投入在这个过程中，你会看到持续的、渐进的进步，而下属掌控着自己的命运。
